title: Macrophage stimulation by bacterial lipopolysaccharides. II. Evidence for differentiation signals delivered by lipid A and by a protein rich fraction of lipopolysaccharides
abstract: This study investigated how lipopolysaccharides (LPS) stimulate macrophages to kill tumor cells. Lipid A and a protein-rich fraction (LAP) both independently deliver signals for macrophage differentiation.

title: The orientation of choroidal macrophage polarization significantly influences the development of myopia in murine models
authors: Jing Hou, Shin-ichi Ikeda, Kiwako Mori, Heonuk Jeong, Hidemasa Torii, Kazuno Negishi, Kazuo Tsubota ...
abstract: Choroidal macrophages were studied for their role in myopia development. Their polarization towards M1 or M2 phenotypes significantly influences choroidal thickness and myopia progression.

title: Macrophage stimulation by bacterial lipopolysaccharides. I. Cytolytic effect on tumor target cells
abstract: Mouse macrophages were stimulated with bacterial lipopolysaccharides to kill tumor cells in vitro. This LPS-induced macrophage cytotoxicity is nonspecific, requires viable effector cells, and is dependent on macrophage density.

title: Comparative Study of The Effect of LPS on The Function of BALB/c and C57BL/6 Peritoneal Macrophages
authors: Sara Soudi; Ahmad Zavaran-Hosseini; Zuhair Muhammad Hassan; Masoud Soleimani; Fatemeh Jamshidi Adega...
abstract: Peritoneal macrophages from BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice were stimulated with LPS to compare their responses. Different mouse strains exhibit distinct cytokine profiles and functional activities when exposed to LPS.

title: Lipopolysaccharide from Porphyromonas gingivalis, but Not from Porphyromonas endodontalis, Induces Macrophage M1 Profile
authors: Pablo Veloso; Alejandra Fernández; Jessica Astorga; David González-Quintanilla; Alfredo Castro; Alej...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of lipopolysaccharides from *Porphyromonas gingivalis* and *Porphyromonas endodontalis* on macrophage polarization. *P. gingivalis* LPS induced an M1 macrophage profile, while *P. endodontalis* LPS did not.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-Activated Macrophages Suppress Cellular Senescence and Promote Rejuvenation in Human Dermal Fibroblasts
authors: Hiroyuki Inagawa; Chie Kohchi; Miyuki Uehiro; Gen-Ichiro Soma
abstract: LPS-activated macrophages were studied for their effect on senescent human dermal fibroblasts. Their secretions suppressed senescence and partially rejuvenated aged fibroblasts.

title: Lipopolysaccharide preconditioning augments the antibacterial activity of renal macrophages and ameliorates acute kidney injury caused by Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia in mice
authors: Keiko Tanoue; Manabu Kinoshita; Bradley M Kearney; Seigo Ito; Hiroyasu Goto; Aoi Yamashiro; Tsugumi ...
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide preconditioning was studied for its effects on renal macrophages and acute kidney injury in mice infected with *Staphylococcus aureus*. Preconditioning enhanced renal macrophage antibacterial activity, reducing bacterial growth and ameliorating kidney injury.

title: A Global Picture of Molecular Changes Associated to LPS Treatment in THP-1 Derived Human Macrophages by Fourier Transform Infrared Microspectroscopy
authors: Diletta Ami; Ana Rita Franco; Valentina Artusa; Paolo Mereghetti; Francesco Peri; Antonino Natalello
abstract: Fourier transform infrared microspectroscopy analyzed THP-1 derived macrophages treated with LPS. The study identified spectral markers in lipids, proteins, and sulfated sugars, highlighting their role in inflammation.

title: LPS adsorption and inflammation alleviation by polymyxin B-modified liposomes for atherosclerosis treatment
authors: Huiwen Liu; Honglan Wang; Qiyu Li; Yiwei Wang; Ying He; Xuejing Li; Chunyan Sun; Onder Ergonul; Füsu...
id: Matched: Inhibitive effect of PLPs on LPS-induced macrophage activation
abstract: Polymyxin B-modified liposomes were developed to adsorb lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for atherosclerosis treatment. This approach reduced inflammation, stabilized plaques, and attenuated atherosclerosis progression by targeting circulating LPS.

title: Lipopolysaccharide from biofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 induces macrophage hyperinflammatory responses
authors: Sufei Wang; Dandan Xiang; Fangbing Tian; Ming Ni
abstract: Biofilm-forming *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* LPS was studied for its effect on macrophage polarization. This LPS induced hyperinflammatory responses and increased bacterial growth in macrophages compared to planktonic LPS.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-induced inflammation in monocytes/macrophages is blocked by liposomal delivery of Gi-protein inhibitor
authors: Monica Madalina Tucureanu; Daniela Rebleanu; Cristina Ana Constantinescu; Mariana Deleanu; Geanina V...
abstract: Liposomes encapsulating a G$_i$-protein inhibitor were tested for anti-inflammatory effects in LPS-activated monocytes/macrophages. Liposomal delivery of the inhibitor effectively blocked LPS-induced inflammation, cytokine production, monocyte adhesion, and chemotaxis.

title: Oral and transdermal administration of lipopolysaccharide safely enhances self-healing ability through the macrophage network
authors: Gen-Ichiro Soma; Masataka Oda; Vindy Tjendana Tjhin; Chie Kohchi; Hiroyuki Inagawa
id: Matched: Regulation of innate immunity by LPS as an environmental agent
abstract: Oral and transdermal LPS administration was studied for its effects on self-healing. This method safely enhances healing through a "macrophage network" involving mucosal immune cells.

title: Exosomal miR-148a-3p from LPS-Activated Macrophages Promotes M1 Polarization and Ferroptosis-Related Characteristics of Recipient Macrophages by Reducing SLC7A11
authors: Jun Liang; Yingli Cai; Yiming Shao
id: Matched: LPS Induces M1 Polarization and Inflammatory Response in RAW264.7 Macr
abstract: Gram-negative bacterial infection is a major cause of severe inflammatory disorders and cellular damage, with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as a key pathogenic trigger. Macrophages are central players in L

title: Transcriptional profiling of the LPS induced NF-κB response in macrophages
authors: Omar Sharif; Viacheslav N Bolshakov; Stephanie Raines; Peter Newham; Neil D Perkins
id: Matched: Analysis of LPS-induced gene expression in the THP-1 macrophage cell l
abstract: This study profiled gene expression in macrophages after LPS exposure. LPS induced a dynamic, time-dependent transcriptional response, with THP-1 cells closely mimicking primary macrophages.

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni; Yanal Ghosheh; Akula Bala Pramod; Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

title: Motif prediction to distinguish LPS-stimulated pro-inflammatory vs. antibacterial macrophage genes
authors: Rahul K Kollipara; Narayanan B Perumal
id: Matched: Classification of antibacterial and pro-inflammatory macrophage genes
abstract: This study analyzed gene expression patterns in LPS-stimulated macrophages to identify pro-inflammatory and antibacterial genes. It found distinct transcription factor binding site motifs associated with each gene set, helping to distinguish their regulatory mechanisms.

title: Mathematical modelling of activation-induced heterogeneity reveals cell state transitions underpinning macrophage responses to LPS
authors: S. Dey, D. Boucher, J. W. Pitchford, D. Lagos *
id: Matched: Macrophage community AIH is dependent on LPS dose
abstract: This study mathematically models macrophage responses to LPS, analyzing single-cell protein expression. Macrophage hypo-responsiveness to secondary LPS challenges is driven by altered transition rates to non-responsive states.

title: Progranulin inhibits LPS-induced macrophage M1 polarization via NF-кB and MAPK pathways
authors: Lianlian Liu; Hongmei Guo; Aimei Song; Jiahui Huang; Yu Zhang; Shanshan Jin; Shutong Li; Liguo Zhang...
id: Matched: Effect of LPS on macrophage M1 polarization and PGRN expression
abstract: Progranulin was studied for its effect on LPS-induced macrophage M1 polarization. Progranulin inhibits M1 polarization by suppressing NF-κB and MAPK pathways.

title: Macrophage–Bacteria Interactions—A Lipid-Centric Relationship
authors: Ooiean Teng; Candice Ke En Ang; Xue Li Guan
abstract: This review examines how macrophages and bacteria interact through lipid metabolism. Manipulating host lipids is a key bacterial strategy, offering potential therapeutic targets for infections.

title: AZD6738 Attenuates LPS-Induced Corneal Inflammation and Fibrosis by Modulating Macrophage Function and Polarization
authors: Longxiang Huang; Youfang Luo
id: Matched: AZD6738 Reduces LPS-induced Corneal Structural Damage and Inhibits Mac
abstract: AZD6738, an ATR inhibitor, was tested in a mouse model of LPS-induced bacterial keratitis. The drug reduced corneal inflammation and fibrosis by modulating macrophage function and polarization.

title: Free Fatty Acids and LPS Synergistically Promote Macrophage M1 Polarization and Insulin Resistance Via FTO-Mediated CSF1 Degradation
authors: Xiaohui Xiao; Junhao Zhao; Guiwen Ye; Hui Li; Xiuji Huang
id: Matched: FFA + LPS Mediates Macrophage M1 Polarization by Upregulating FTO
abstract: This study investigated how free fatty acids and LPS promote macrophage M1 polarization and insulin resistance. These factors synergistically induce insulin resistance by promoting M1 polarization via FTO-mediated CSF1 degradation.

title: BRD4 contributes to LPS-induced macrophage senescence and promotes progression of atherosclerosis-associated lipid uptake
authors: Hui Wang; Haiping Fu; Ruigong Zhu; Xuan Wu; Xian Ji; Xuesong Li; Hong Jiang; Zhe Lin; Xin Tang; Shix...
id: Matched: BRD4 is indispensable for LPS-induced peritoneal macrophage senescence
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induces macrophage senescence, which is mediated by BRD4. Inhibiting BRD4 prevents LPS-induced macrophage senescence and lipid accumulation, suggesting therapeutic potential for atherosclerosis.

title: Species-Specificity of Transcriptional Regulation and the Response to Lipopolysaccharide in Mammalian Macrophages
authors: Stephen J. Bush; Mary E. B. McCulloch; Zofia M. Lisowski; Charity Muriuki; Emily L. Clark; Rachel Yo...
abstract: This study analyzed the transcriptional response of sheep macrophages to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and compared it to other mammalian species. A conserved transcriptional network was found, but large animals and rodents differed in their metabolic responses to LPS.

title: A host lipase prevents lipopolysaccharide-induced foam cell formation
authors: Jintao Feng; Wei Jiang; Xiaofang Cheng; Benkun Zou; Alan W. Varley; Ting Liu; Guojun Qian; Wenjiao Z...
id: Matched: LPS-exposed Aoah−/− peritoneal macrophages accumulate more cholesterol
abstract: A host lipase, acyloxyacyl hydrolase (AOAH), was studied for its role in preventing lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced foam cell formation. AOAH inactivates LPS, and its absence leads to increased cholesterol accumulation and inflammation in macrophages.

title: Translation control of TAK1 mRNA by hnRNP K modulates LPS-induced macrophage activation
authors: Anke Liepelt; Jana C. Mossanen; Bernd Denecke; Felix Heymann; Rebecca De Santis; Frank Tacke; Gernot...
id: Matched: Identification of hnRNP K-associated mRNAs affected in macrophage LPS
abstract: This study investigated how hnRNP K regulates TAK1 mRNA translation. Macrophage activation releases hnRNP K, relieving repression and promoting TAK1 synthesis for an inflammatory response.
